response.title: Harborlight FY2026 Results and a Sixth Site

segments.heading: The learners we served
segments.text: Harborlight grew in fiscal year 2026. Staff now ask the board to pay for a sixth site. We start with the learners. Harborlight enrolled 1,148 adult learners at five neighborhood sites. The year before, it enrolled 936. Of these learners, 412 worked toward a high school equivalency credential. And 389 were English language learners. Sixty-eight percent of learners who stayed at least 12 weeks gained one or more reading levels on the CASAS assessment. Seventy-one learners earned a high school equivalency credential. That is the most in the organization's history.

segments.heading: Tutors, staff and money
segments.text: Next come people and money. A team of 214 volunteer tutors gave 9,870 tutoring hours. On average, a tutor stayed 14 months. Harborlight has 11 full-time staff, and four of them are site coordinators. Operating expenses for FY2026 came to $1,420,000. Programs made up 81 percent of spending. Foundation grants brought in $640,000. Individual donors gave $388,000. The city's adult education contract paid $295,000. The cost per learner was $1,237.

segments.heading: Adults still waiting
segments.text: Now to the waitlist. At year end, 287 adults were on the waitlist. Most of them were at the Eastgate and Riverside sites. The average wait was nine weeks. These adults want to learn, and they have not found a seat yet. A learner at the Riverside site shared what this work can mean. Quote: "I read my granddaughter a bedtime story for the first time this spring." End quote.

segments.heading: What staff recommend
segments.text: Here is what staff recommend. They ask the board to approve an FY2027 budget of $1,610,000. The budget adds a sixth site at the Eastgate branch library. It also adds two site coordinators. Eastgate is one of the two sites where most waitlisted adults are. Staff estimate the new site would serve 180 more learners a year. They also estimate it would cut the waitlist in half.

segments.heading: Reserves and next steps
segments.text: Last, reserves and next steps. The board held a retreat on September 13. At the retreat, treasurer Dev Patel reported that reserves stand at 3.2 months of operating expenses. That falls short of the board's target of 4 months. The board asked staff to bring a one-page summary of the FY2027 budget request to the October 21 board meeting. Board members also asked for a short deck to use with funders when they talk about the sixth site. The board agreed to vote on the FY2027 budget on October 21.

response.recap: Keep three things in mind. First, Harborlight enrolled 1,148 adult learners in FY2026, and seventy-one earned a high school equivalency credential. Second, 287 adults were on the waitlist at year end, and the average wait was nine weeks. Third, staff recommend an FY2027 budget of $1,610,000 for a sixth site. Reserves stand at 3.2 months, short of the board's target of 4 months.
